en.headline: Youth arrests rise 23 per cent in first eight months, police chief says
en.dek: Commissioner Joe Chow disclosed the figure while officiating a civic education ceremony, linking most cases to impulsive assaults, fraud involving bank accounts, and damage tied to debt collection.
body: Commissioner of Police Joe Chow Yat-ming said on Saturday that 2,144 young people had been arrested for criminal offences in the first eight months of the year, a 23 per cent increase from the same period last year.

Speaking at the graduation ceremony for the third Hong Kong Inter-School Civic Education Officer Selection Competition at Police Headquarters in Wan Chai, Chow said the main offences were wounding and serious assault arising from minor disputes, deception and money laundering in which young people acted as runners or lent out bank accounts, and criminal damage linked to illegal debt collection or schemes promising quick money.

He stressed that the force places high importance on raising young people’s awareness of the law and their ability to recognise traps. The police have issued the latest edition of a guide for parents and teachers that breaks down emerging crime methods and common misconceptions, and will continue training sessions by specialised units.

The competition this year drew more than 1,100 students from 120 schools; after selection and three months of training, 100 were appointed as civic education officers. Organisers hope to expand the programme to the Greater Bay Area next year.

zh.headline: 首八月逾2100名青少年被捕按年升23% 周一鳴：加強防罪宣傳
zh.dek: 警務處處長周一鳴在學界公民教育專員畢業禮上披露數據，指主要涉及傷人毆打、詐騙洗黑錢及與非法收債有關的刑事毀壞。
body: 警務處處長周一鳴周六表示，今年首八個月共有2144名青少年因觸犯刑事罪行被捕，較去年同期上升23%。
他在灣仔警察總部出席第三屆「全港學界公民教育專員選拔賽」畢業暨頒獎禮時指出，主要罪行包括因瑣事糾紛一時衝動而干犯的傷人及嚴重毆打、涉及借出戶口或充當「跑腿」的詐騙及洗黑錢，以及與非法收債或「賺快錢」有關的刑事毀壞。
周一鳴強調，警隊高度重視提升青少年守法意識及防罪能力。警方剛發布最新一期《師長攻略•青少年陷阱解密》，拆解各類新興手法及認知誤區，並會繼續由網罪科等單位向學生提供培訓。
本屆選拔賽吸引逾1100名來自120間學校的中小學生參與，經培訓後100人獲委任為公民教育專員。主辦方期望明年將活動拓展至粵港澳大灣區。
